```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)

set.seed(1)
```

## Airbnb

```{r}
data("nyc_airbnb")

nyc_airbnb =
  nyc_airbnb |> 
  mutate(
    stars = review_scores_location / 2
  ) |> 
  rename(
    borough = neighbourhood_group,
    neighborhood = neighbourhood
  ) |> 
  filter(
    borough != "Staten Island"
  ) |> 
  select(price, stars, borough, neighborhood, room_type)
```

Fit a linear regression!

```{r}
fit = lm(price ~ stars + borough, data = nyc_airbnb)
```

Look at what we have

```{r}
fit
summary(fit)
coef(fit)
fitted.values(fit)
resid(fit)

names(fit)
names(summary(fit))
```

most of this output is bad, but sometimes it's okay

let's do better

```{r}
broom::tidy(fit)
```

pulls out the coefficients and SE, p-value, formatted as a data frame

Let's further format it!

```{r}
broom::tidy(fit) |> 
  select(-std.error) |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

broom::glance(fit)
```

Bronx is the current reference category because it's the first in the alphabetical (and we can tell by it not being there in the table)

Change reference category

```{r}
fit = 
  nyc_airbnb |> 
  mutate(borough = fct_infreq(borough)) |> 
  lm(price ~ stars + borough, data = _)

broom::tidy(fit) |> 
  select(-std.error, -statistic) |> 
  mutate(term = str_replace(term, "borough", "Borough: ")) |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```
